text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Aneurysm imaging: duplex ultrasound today and CT angiography within two weeks for baseline anatomy; then duplex ultrasound every six months while the diameter is 5.0 to 5.4 cm, with CT if ultrasound views are poor
  • Vascular surgery consultation for a shared decision about surveillance, repair thresholds, and the choice between endovascular and open repair
  • Blood pressure below 130/80: add losartan 50 mg to amlodipine, home blood pressure readings twice daily for a week before each visit, and a metabolic panel two to four weeks after each change, then every six months
  • Atorvastatin 40 mg each evening, with a baseline ALT and a lipid panel four to twelve weeks after starting, then yearly
  • Tobacco cessation: the 5 A's at every visit, a quit date within a week, a 14 mg nicotine patch with 2 mg lozenges for cravings, stepping down over the following months, and the state quitline
  • Emergency plan: sudden severe abdominal, back, flank, or groin pain, fainting, or a tender pulsating lump means calling emergency services at once; carry an aneurysm wallet card; avoid fluoroquinolone antibiotics unless there is no alternative
  • Low-dose aspirin 81 mg daily for atheroma of the aorta, unless bleeding risk outweighs benefit
  • Shared decision on elective repair: repair advised at 5.5 cm by a consistent measurement, growth of 0.5 cm or more in six months, or symptoms from the aneurysm; endovascular repair favored on this anatomy and after a prior laparotomy with wrapping; his preferences reviewed at each scan
  • Monitor on the CMID hypertension and hyperlipidemia schedules: blood pressure and weight at every visit; metabolic panel every six months on losartan; lipids, HbA1c, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio yearly; baseline ECG; eye examination yearly; ankle-brachial index every two to three years

resource.title: Albert Einstein synthetic care plan
resource.description: First six months of care of a 70-year-old man with an infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm below the repair threshold, known since an exploratory laparotomy at which it was wrapped rather than repaired: baseline duplex ultrasound and CT angiography, surveillance every six months at 5.0 to 5.4 cm, blood pressure below 130/80, a high-intensity statin, low-dose aspirin for aortic atheroma, smoking cessation with nicotine replacement, avoidance of fluoroquinolones, education about symptoms that need emergency care, and a documented shared decision with vascular surgery about elective repair thresholds (5.5 cm in men, rapid growth, or symptoms) and endovascular versus open repair, following the Society for Vascular Surgery 1941 and ACC/AHA 1945 guidelines with the CMID hypertension and hyperlipidemia monographs. His preferences are recorded as synthetic shared decision-making; the decision he made at the end of his life is history only.
